basic_information.name: Unstructured.io
basic_information.creator: Unstructured Technologies, Inc. (founded by Brian Raymond)
basic_information.description: Unstructured.io is an open-source ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) platform for converting complex unstructured documents into clean, structured formats optimized for LLMs and RAG pipelines. It partitions documents from 30+ file types into semantic elements (Title, NarrativeText, Table, ListItem, PageBreak, Image), enriches them with layout ML models for table detection, header recognition, and OCR, and outputs structured JSON, Markdown, HTML, or Arrow formats with metadata including coordinates, page numbers, languages, and SHA hashes. With 71+ pre-built connectors spanning cloud storage, collaboration platforms, vector databases, and LLM providers, it enables 1,250+ unique source-to-destination data pipelines. Trusted by 35,000+ companies and government organizations (including McKinsey, BlackRock, U.S. Air Force), Unstructured addresses the critical 'first mile' problem in enterprise GenAI: transforming messy, heterogeneous documents into AI-ready data at scale.
basic_information.release_date: First commit in 2022; commercial SaaS API launched January 2024; v0.18 series (summer 2025) with faster PDF partitioning and revamped chunking API
basic_information.license: Apache 2.0 (open-source library). Note: some dependencies (ultralytics, chardet) use AGPL/LGPL licenses which has raised compatibility concerns. Enterprise platform is proprietary (open-core model).

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Library + API + Platform (hybrid). The open-source Python library runs locally or in containers. The hosted Unstructured Platform provides a serverless API with pay-as-you-go compute. Enterprise deployments support dedicated instances, VPC hosting, or customer-managed VPC. Processing strategies: FAST (pdfminer + heuristics, seconds per document) and HI_RES (Chipper layout model for page-level accuracy, ~20x slower, optional GPU). The platform uses a DAG-based workflow engine for orchestrating multi-step ingestion pipelines.
technical_architecture.language: Python (primary). SDKs: Python client (unstructured-client), JavaScript/TypeScript client. Internal ML models use PyTorch. CLI tool (unstructured-ingest) for batch processing.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Not an embedding model itself — Unstructured is a document processing/partitioning tool. However, the platform integrates embedding as a pipeline step, supporting OpenAI, Cohere, HuggingFace, and other embedding models with configurable dimensions. The chunked output is designed to be embedded by any downstream model.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — Unstructured is a document processing tool, not a vector database. It does not perform vector indexing. Instead, it outputs structured chunks that are loaded into vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Qdrant, Chroma, LanceDB, etc.) which handle their own indexing.
technical_architecture.scalability: Platform supports horizontal scaling with configurable concurrency levels. Batches of 2-20 pages can be processed in parallel. Enterprise platform offers infinite scaling based on infrastructure capacity. The Ingest CLI supports multi-file batch processing with parallel workers. A single complex PDF page can generate hundreds of thousands of Python objects, so GPU acceleration is recommended for HI_RES strategy at scale.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted (pip install, Docker), Unstructured SaaS API (hosted cloud), Unstructured Platform (managed UI + API), Enterprise dedicated instance (VPC deployment), customer-managed VPC. Docker images available for local containerized deployment. Kubernetes-compatible for enterprise orchestration.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: N/A — Unstructured is a document processing/ingestion tool, not a retrieval engine. It prepares documents for retrieval by partitioning and structuring content. The structured output (elements with metadata, coordinates, page numbers) is then ingested into vector databases or search engines that perform the actual retrieval. Unstructured is the 'E' and 'T' in ETL, not the query/retrieval layer.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Two built-in chunking strategies: (1) 'basic' — combines sequential elements to fill chunks up to max_characters (hard-max, default 500) and new_after_n_chars (soft-max), with configurable overlap for text-splitting at oversized elements; (2) 'by_title' — document-structure-aware chunking that preserves section boundaries and optionally page boundaries, never combining text from different sections. Both strategies operate on pre-partitioned document elements (not raw text), making them inherently structure-aware. Key parameters: max_characters, new_after_n_chars, overlap, combine_text_under_n_chars. The approach is semantically superior to naive text-splitting because partitioning first identifies logical document units (titles, paragraphs, tables, lists) before chunking.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: No built-in reranking. Unstructured focuses on document processing/ingestion rather than query-time retrieval. Reranking is handled by downstream components (vector databases, LangChain/LlamaIndex pipelines, or dedicated rerankers like Cohere Rerank, cross-encoders).
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Strong multimodal document processing: OCR for scanned documents and images (via Tesseract and PaddleOCR), table extraction with ML-based table detection models, image element extraction from documents, chart and figure identification. The HI_RES strategy uses the Chipper vision-language model for page-layout analysis. Supports extracting images, tables, and charts as separate elements with bounding box coordinates. Integration with NVIDIA NeMo Retriever microservices for up to 15x faster multimodal preprocessing. Output includes element-level metadata for downstream multimodal RAG pipelines.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No built-in knowledge graph construction. However, Unstructured integrates with Neo4j AuraDB for building document knowledge graphs from partitioned elements. The structured element output (with titles, sections, relationships) provides good raw material for entity extraction and graph construction. Users combine Unstructured partitioning with entity extraction tools (spaCy, LLM-based) to populate knowledge graphs.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Element-level metadata provides strong grounding capabilities: each partitioned element includes source filename, page number, element type, coordinates (bounding boxes), section hierarchy, and SHA-256 hash. This metadata enables downstream RAG systems to implement precise source attribution and citation, linking generated answers back to specific pages, sections, and even pixel coordinates in source documents. No built-in LLM-based citation verification.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Chunking strategies (basic and by_title) directly address context window limits by producing right-sized chunks. The max_characters parameter controls chunk size to fit within embedding model and LLM context windows. Overlap parameter ensures semantic continuity across chunk boundaries. Document-structure-aware chunking (by_title) naturally produces more coherent chunks that make better use of context window space. No built-in summarization or compression — these are handled by downstream orchestrators.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Highly variable by strategy and document complexity. FAST strategy: seconds per document (uses pdfminer + heuristics). HI_RES strategy: ~20x slower than FAST (uses ML-based layout detection, optional GPU). A single complex PDF page can generate hundreds of thousands of Python objects. Specific p50/p99 latency metrics are not publicly published. The platform supports configurable concurrency and batching (2-20 pages per batch) to improve throughput. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Not publicly benchmarked with specific pages-per-second metrics. Throughput depends on: processing strategy (FAST vs HI_RES), document complexity, hardware (CPU vs GPU), concurrency settings, and whether using local library vs hosted API. The platform's serverless architecture scales compute dynamically. Codeflash partnership (2025) reported significant pipeline acceleration through Python performance optimization. Enterprise platform claims 'infinite scaling based on infrastructure capacity'. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: In third-party PDF extraction benchmarks (Procycons 2025): achieved 100% accuracy on simple table extraction but only 75% on complex tables. Unstructured's own blog claims leadership in document parsing quality benchmarks across diverse document types. Accuracy varies significantly by document type and processing strategy — HI_RES with Chipper model provides substantially better layout fidelity than FAST. No single published MTEB or BEIR score (not an embedding/retrieval model). [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Third-party comparison (Procycons 2025 benchmark, Reducto comparison): Unstructured provides strong OCR capabilities and broad file format support but produces incomplete or incorrect extraction in some complex cases, requiring post-processing. Docling (IBM) and LlamaParse scored higher on complex table extraction accuracy. Unstructured's strength is breadth (30+ file types, 71+ connectors) rather than best-in-class accuracy on any single format. Unstructured's own benchmark blog counters that quality depends heavily on configuration and that their latest models outperform competitors on diverse real-world document sets. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Deep integrations with major RAG orchestration frameworks: LangChain (UnstructuredFileLoader via langchain-unstructured package, DirectoryLoader), LlamaIndex (UnstructuredReader in llama-index-readers-file), Haystack (supported as document converter). Also integrates with Ray for distributed processing pipelines, Elasticsearch for search, and Databricks for data engineering workflows. The Unstructured Ingest CLI provides framework-agnostic batch processing.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Framework-agnostic for LLMs — Unstructured processes documents independently of the generation model. The platform's embedding step supports OpenAI, Cohere, HuggingFace, and other embedding providers. Output integrates with any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, open-source models) through downstream orchestrators. NVIDIA partnership provides accelerated processing via NeMo Retriever microservices.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes — official MCP server available (github.com/Unstructured-IO/UNS-MCP). Launched April 2025. Provides tools to list/manage sources, destinations, workflows, and jobs through the Model Context Protocol. Compatible with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP-enabled LLM clients. Documentation and hands-on walkthroughs available. Unstructured hosted an MCP Virtual Hackathon to encourage adoption.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: 71+ pre-built connectors enabling 1,250+ unique pipelines. Source connectors include: Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, Box, Dropbox, OneDrive, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Slack, Discord, GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, Elasticsearch, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Reddit, Wikipedia, web crawlers (including Firecrawl integration), SFTP, local filesystem. Destination connectors include: Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus/Zilliz, Qdrant, Chroma, LanceDB, KDB.AI, Astra DB, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, MongoDB Atlas, PostgreSQL (pgvector), Delta Lake, Databricks Volumes, S3, Azure, GCS. Enterprise platform: 30 enterprise-grade connectors (15 sources + 15 destinations) with rapid expansion.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: The Unstructured Platform provides built-in observability through the Jobs view (workflow run results, error tracking). Bounding box visualization for document element verification. Side-by-side original vs. transformed document rendering. No direct integration with third-party LLM observability platforms (LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix) — observability of the downstream RAG pipeline is handled by the orchestration framework. Platform API provides programmatic access to job status and results. [uncertain]

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model. Free: open-source Python library (unlimited local processing). Paid: (1) 'Let's Go' — free tier with 15,000 pages, no expiration; (2) 'Pay-As-You-Go' — flat rate per compute hour ($2.66/hour), no minimums or maximums; (3) 'Business' — multi-user, multi-workspace, SaaS or dedicated/VPC options, custom pricing; (4) 'Enterprise' — full data isolation, dedicated support, role-based access, compliance features, custom pricing.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: 15,000 pages free with no expiration date, full access to every platform feature. The open-source library is entirely free with no page limits for self-hosted processing.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Pay-As-You-Go: $2.66/hour of compute. Example: moderate API usage (~1 hour/day) costs ~$79.80/month. For large-scale enterprise processing, costs depend on document volume, complexity, and processing strategy (HI_RES costs more compute time than FAST). Self-hosted open-source library has zero licensing cost — only infrastructure (compute, storage) costs. Enterprise and Business tiers have custom pricing based on volume and deployment model. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted (open-source): infrastructure costs only — CPU/GPU servers, storage, maintenance labor. Budget $0 for software, $500-5,000/month for cloud compute depending on volume and GPU needs. Platform (Pay-As-You-Go): $2.66/hour compute + minimal storage. For moderate use (~30 hours/month): ~$80/month. For heavy use (~200 hours/month): ~$530/month. Enterprise (VPC/dedicated): custom pricing, typically $2,000-10,000+/month depending on scale. Hidden costs: GPU instances for HI_RES strategy, storage for source documents, downstream embedding and vector DB costs (not included in Unstructured pricing). The open-source path requires ML engineering expertise for deployment and maintenance. [uncertain]

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the open-source document processing/ingestion category for GenAI and RAG. Named to Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies list in both 2024 and 2025 (#24 in 2025). Included in Forbes AI 50 (2024). Dominant in the 'first mile' data preparation space for enterprise GenAI. Used by 82% of the Fortune 1000 and 60,000+ organizations globally (per company claims). Over 1,000 paying customers as of early 2024.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: McKinsey & Company, BlackRock, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Space Force, United States Special Operations Command, IBM (partnership), NVIDIA (partnership and investor), Databricks (partnership and investor). Fast Company's 2024 recognition highlighted data preparation for AI as their core innovation.
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: ~13,800 stars, ~1,100 forks on main repository. 41 repositories in the Unstructured-IO GitHub organization. Active Slack developer community (exact member count not public). PyPI: 4 million+ cumulative downloads (as of 2023, likely significantly higher by 2026). LinkedIn: active company page. Community repository (Unstructured-IO/community) for open-source collaboration.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: $65 million. Series B: $40 million (March 14, 2024) led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Databricks Ventures, IBM Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA), Sacramento Kings Chairman Vivek Ranadive, Datastax CEO Chet Kapoor, Allison Pickens (New Normal Fund), and existing investors Madrona, Bain Capital Ventures, Mango Capital. Post-money valuation: $230 million (March 2024). Series A: $25 million (2023) led by Bain Capital Ventures.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Docling (IBM Research, open-source, strong table extraction), LlamaParse (LlamaIndex, cloud API, fast processing ~6s per document, natural language instructions), Reducto (cloud API with comparison tools), Apache Tika (legacy open-source document extraction). Cloud document AI competitors: AWS Textract, Google Document AI, Azure Document Intelligence. Key differentiators for Unstructured: broadest file type support (30+ types), largest connector ecosystem (71+ connectors), open-source core with enterprise overlay, document-structure-aware chunking. Weaknesses: accuracy on complex tables lags Docling/LlamaParse in some benchmarks, HI_RES strategy is slow without GPU, open-source version requires significant setup.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for startups building RAG-powered products that need to ingest diverse document types from multiple sources. Best fit: (1) Teams of 2-5 engineers building document Q&A, knowledge management, or compliance tools, (2) B2B SaaS products that must process customer-uploaded documents (contracts, reports, manuals), (3) Startups needing to connect 5+ data sources into a unified RAG pipeline. Budget guidance: Start with the open-source library for POC (free), graduate to Pay-As-You-Go platform (~$80-500/month) for production, consider Enterprise for regulated industries. The 15,000-page free tier is generous enough for most MVPs. Less ideal for: teams processing only one document type (overkill), startups needing real-time sub-second processing (HI_RES is slow), or teams without Python engineering capability.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use open-source library (self-host) when: team has ML engineering skills, need full control over processing pipeline, budget-constrained, processing simple document types, or need air-gapped deployment. Use Unstructured Platform (buy) when: team lacks document processing expertise, need 71+ connectors out of the box, processing diverse/complex document types, need no-code workflow builder, or require compliance features (SOC2, HIPAA). Hybrid approach: use open-source for development and testing, platform for production processing. Key tradeoff: self-hosted is free but requires GPU infrastructure for HI_RES strategy and ongoing maintenance; platform costs $2.66/hour but handles scaling and infrastructure.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-2 days with the open-source library (pip install, basic partitioning). Platform POC: 1-3 days using the no-code UI workflow builder. Production deployment: 2-4 weeks including connector setup, chunking optimization, quality validation with bounding box visualization, and integration with downstream vector DB and LLM. Complex enterprise deployments with multiple sources, compliance requirements, and custom processing: 4-8 weeks. The no-code workflow builder significantly accelerates time-to-production for non-ML teams.
key_lessons: Start with the FAST processing strategy and only switch to HI_RES when document complexity demands it — HI_RES is 20x slower and requires GPU, but many documents (plain text, simple PDFs, HTML) process perfectly with FAST. Profile your document corpus before committing to infrastructure.

Use 'by_title' chunking instead of 'basic' for RAG applications — structure-aware chunking that respects section boundaries produces significantly more coherent chunks, improving retrieval accuracy. The default max_characters of 500 is a good starting point but should be tuned to your embedding model's sweet spot.

Leverage the 71+ pre-built connectors rather than building custom ingestion — the connector ecosystem is Unstructured's strongest differentiator over competitors. Building even one production-grade S3 or Confluence connector from scratch takes weeks.

Validate extraction quality visually before scaling — the platform's bounding box visualization and side-by-side rendering catch extraction errors that automated metrics miss. Invest 1-2 days in manual quality review of representative documents before processing your full corpus.

Consider a hybrid parsing strategy for complex document sets — no single tool excels at everything. Use Unstructured for its breadth (30+ file types, connectors) but consider Docling or LlamaParse for documents with complex tables where accuracy is critical. The output formats are compatible enough to merge into a single RAG pipeline.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — the Unstructured Platform provides a no-code, point-and-click web UI with a visual workflow builder (DAG-based), side-by-side document rendering, bounding box visualization, connector management, and one-click deployment to production. Custom workflow support was added in Q1 2025. The UI supports previewing processing results before scaling.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — data pipeline architecture, build vs buy decisions for document processing) and Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — the no-code workflow builder is directly relevant)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official website, GitHub repository, major tech press (Fast Company, SiliconANGLE, BusinessWire), Crunchbase, and third-party benchmarks. Funding and customer data from authoritative business press.
confidence.cross_reference: Funding details confirmed across BusinessWire (official press release), Crunchbase, SiliconANGLE, Tracxn, and FinSMES. GitHub stars cross-referenced between search results and repository page. Customer claims from official website corroborated by Fast Company and Forbes coverage. Benchmark results from independent third parties (Procycons, Reducto).
confidence.caveats: Customer and adoption numbers (35,000+ companies, 82% Fortune 1000, 60,000+ organizations) are self-reported by Unstructured and could not be independently verified. Benchmark accuracy varies significantly by document type and processing configuration — third-party benchmarks show mixed results vs. competitors on complex tables. The open-source library's Apache 2.0 license has compatibility concerns with AGPL-licensed dependencies. Pricing details for enterprise tier are not publicly available. The market is rapidly evolving with IBM's Docling and LlamaIndex's LlamaParse gaining ground.
confidence.security_posture: SOC 2 Type 1 completed; SOC 2 Type 2 in progress (as of 2025). HIPAA, GDPR, and ISO 27001 compliance available on Plus+ business tier. Data encrypted at rest using cloud-native encryption (Azure Storage Service Encryption, AWS S3 SSE). Authentication via Keycloak with OAuth2/OpenID Connect and external IdP support (Azure AD). Enterprise tier offers full data isolation via dedicated VPC or customer-managed VPC. For the open-source library running self-hosted, security is the user's responsibility. Known considerations: document processing involves parsing potentially malicious files (adversarial PDFs, macro-enabled Office docs), so sandboxed processing environments are recommended for untrusted documents.
